correctness.rationale: Ahn's Pierce normalization reduces every point of \(C\) to a finite rational prefix plus a scaled consecutive tail. The beta-integral identity, integration-by-parts recurrence, and derangement induction are exact for every integer \(m\ge1\). The final \(e^{-1}\)-coefficient is a nonzero rational, so Hermite's transcendence theorem for \(e\) gives transcendence of every point. The included verifier corroborates recurrence and gluing formulas without being used as an infinite proof.

Ahn supplies the symbolic/topological exceptional set but not its arithmetic evaluation; Varona's recurrence-based theorem does not cover general consecutive tails; Shallit treats a different explicit quadratic family.

value.rationale: The source paper's main homeomorphism excludes exactly \(C\), so determining the arithmetic nature of all excluded points directly sharpens its structural interpretation. The theorem gives a closed form for every exceptional point and the natural consequence that all algebraic irrationals remain in the image; this is broader and more motivated than evaluating a single named Pierce series.
